title: Set a wristwatch to 10:10: crown out to the time click, turned in strokes, pushed back in, the date left as it was
instruction: Set the watch on the stand to 10:10 without changing its date, and leave its crown pushed fully in.
context: Setting an analogue watch is something most people do by hand: twice a year for daylight saving time, after a battery change, or when it has drifted; watch shops set the watches on display to 10:10. Timex's guide (How to Set the Time on Any Watch): the crown is "pulled out as far as it will go" (some watches have "two or three 'stops'"), turned to set the hands, then "push the crown back to its starting position"; "Make sure the crown is pushed all the way back in when you're done." On a date watch the first stop sets the date. The hand skill: the crown is 5.5 mm across and stands 4 mm out from the case, so the fingertips can take it only by its end; it is drawn out past two clicks 0.9 mm apart without turning it at the first (the date); it needs two full turns, made in strokes (grip, turn, let go, turn back) and stopped within 30 deg of the crown (one minute); then it is pushed home past both clicks. One arm is enough: the stand holds the watch.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Single-watch display stand, fixed (taped down): base plate 9 x 7 x 0.6 cm centred at x 28, y 0; a post 1.2 cm across; an oval C-ring 6.4 cm wide (along x), 5.0 cm tall, 2.6 cm deep (along y), 3 mm thick, its top 13.5 cm above the table. (2) Quartz three-hand wristwatch with a date window (like a Timex Easy Reader Date 38 mm), about 40 g: steel case 38 mm across and 9.5 mm thick, white dial, 20 mm brown leather strap buckled round the ring; dial up, centred over x 28, y 0, 12 o'clock toward +x, the crown (5.5 mm across, 4 mm long, its axis 14.0 cm above the table, centred at x 28, y -2.15 when pushed in) toward -y. Battery out, so the hands move only when the crown turns them. Hands at 9:46, crown pushed in. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every control step: the crown's position and turn and each finger's collision points. Hands read on the 12-hour dial. 0.25 the crown has been out at its 2nd click (time) at some time; 0.5 the hands read within 5 min of 10:10; 0.75 within 1 min of 10:10, the date unchanged; 1.0 (success, held 1 s) as 0.75 with the crown pushed fully home (nearer home than the 1st click) and every finger point 1 cm or more from the watch head. Once the date has been changed (half a turn of the crown at the 1st click) the score is at most 0.5. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: a photo of the dial at the end (minute hand within one minute mark of the 2, hour hand just past 10; the date as at the start); the crown home is checked after the photo by turning it gently without pulling: home, it moves neither the hands nor the date.
reset_notes: Pull the crown to the time click, set the hands to 9:46 (coming up to it), push the crown fully in, check the date (set it back at the date click if it changed), and buckle the watch on the ring dial up with the crown toward the robot's right. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The watch head is boxes and cylinders at true size; the strap is drawn only and the watch is held fixed on its ring. The movement is not simulated: the stem slides on a spring toward its nearest click (1.5 N peak), the crown turns against 1.5 mN m, and in the 2nd click the hands are driven at 12 min per crown turn; half a crown turn at the 1st click counts as a date change (estimates). The date disc is not drawn.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper came over the watch from above early on, then both arms hung back low beside the stand; the crown was never pulled out and the hands stayed at 9:46); demo: 1.0
